figures.caption: Fig. 1: Success against inference cost. Success rate on the 18 RoboCasa tasks versus inference frequency and energy per inference. DEM reaches success comparable to the VLMbackbone VLAs at a fraction of their cost.

Fig. 2: Conventional VLA versus DEM. Left: a conventional VLA (π0.5 [4]) routes images and instruction through one VLM and generates actions by multi-step flow matching; the instruction is re-encoded at every step. Right: DEM encodes images with DINOv3 ConvNeXt-B and the instruction with NeoBERT, fuses them by cross-attention inside the action head, and generates the chunk with MeanFlow in one forward pass. The dashed language pathway runs only when the instruction changes. Boxes give per-stage latencies and sum to the figures of Table II.
Fig. 3: Simulated tasks. One demonstration frame per task, grouped by the skill categories of Table I.

TABLE I: RoboCasa success rate (%). 18 tasks, 100 rollouts each, grouped by the eight RoboCasa skill categories [36] (task counts in parentheses); a category score is the mean over its tasks and Avg. the mean over all 18. The blender lid and stand-mixer head are counted with doors. All policies fine-tuned on the same demonstrations for 300k steps; standard error up to 5 points per task and about 1.2 points for Avg. Best in bold.
